heading: Terminology
text: Terminology

heading: Terminology
text: **Module instance:** One Runtime-known realization of a module owned by exactly one Runtime. It has one Runtime-scoped instance identity, one Runtime-owned lifecycle, and optional persistent-state, placement, presentation, and provider state. The owning Runtime controls its Logos lifecycle semantics. A module instance identity MAY remain stable across stop/start cycles when the Runtime host or deployment preserves that identity.

heading: Terminology
text: **Consumer:** The module instance whose authority is used for an operation. Runtime authenticates the consumer at the invocation boundary. A route is established for exactly one consumer, and only that module instance may use it. Consumer is a relationship in an operation or route rather than a separately managed entity. A module-instance address identifies the consumer. The address does not authenticate the module instance or grant authority. Runtime MUST preserve the addressed module-instance identity while it is needed to keep active routes and retained authority or audit material unambiguous.

heading: Terminology
text: If a later specification needs a human, user-session, device, organization, or agent identity, it must define that identity and its delegation relationship explicitly.

heading: Terminology
text: When a module performs an operation, Runtime binds that module instance as the consumer and active authority policy must permit the consumer and requested operation.

heading: Terminology
text: Changing execution mode MUST NOT silently change the module interface contract observed by callers.

heading: Terminology
text: Every system service provider MUST be a local module provider backed by a local module instance.

heading: Terminology
text: Runtime MUST maintain ordinary provider and lifecycle records for their module instances.

heading: Terminology
text: A system service provider MAY use direct mode or local transport mode according to active policy and the applicable profile.

heading: Terminology
text: An implementation MAY co-locate or statically link system service code, but Runtime MUST represent that code as a direct-mode local module instance and preserve its provider, lifecycle, system-service binding, and authority records.

heading: Terminology
text: Remote facades and external host or deployment services MUST NOT be bound as system service providers in this revision.

heading: 8.1 Module Initialization Inputs

heading: 8.1 Module Initialization Inputs
text: Runtime MUST NOT initiate graceful release while another instance-dependent call is in flight.

heading: 8.1 Module Initialization Inputs

text: 9. Runtime-Control Interface

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST accept a Runtime Control invocation only from an authenticated module instance.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST authorize the consumer and requested method, target, and observation scope according to active policy before executing an operation, except that `report_failure` uses the caller-bound authorization rule in Section 9.3.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A runtime instance MUST have an authority policy for runtime-control operations, route establishment, system service access, provider visibility, lifecycle control, and remote-runtime enrollment.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Before Runtime binds an initial system service provider, Runtime MUST have bootstrap authority policy established by its runtime host or deployment inputs.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Bootstrap policy MAY identify initial system service providers and grant only the operations needed to validate and reach those providers.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A candidate provider MUST NOT select, bind, or authorize itself as an authority-bearing system service.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST authorize each initial system service binding from bootstrap policy rather than from the candidate provider or another provider that is not yet bound.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime startup MUST establish the initial orchestration realization under bootstrap policy.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When Module Loader is used, its initial provider MUST be established first and used to realize orchestration.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When authority policy is externalized, bootstrap policy MUST identify the orchestration instance and the operations and targets it may use to establish the selected initial Capability Authority.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface

text: Before using a local-transport system service provider, Runtime MUST complete the authorized Transport Hello exchange for the required module contract under LOGOS-MODULE-TRANSPORT Section 8.1.2.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST NOT use the provider for dependent operations until all binding checks succeed.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If an external Capability Authority is unavailable, Runtime MUST deny operations that depend on it unless bootstrap policy defines a narrower recovery path.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If no authority policy allows an operation, the runtime MUST deny the operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: For authority-policy evaluation, Runtime MUST authenticate the consumer at the enforcement boundary and use the consumer identity defined by LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MAY derive policy attributes from authenticated context.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST populate or validate the Capability Authority request's `consumer` against the authenticated consumer for the attempted operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST reject a returned decision whose consumer does not match the request.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When authority policy denies an operation, the runtime MUST NOT perform the operation and MUST report an authorization failure through the method, transport, or runtime API error channel used for the attempted operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST fail closed for the attempted operation, but it MUST NOT record an authority-evaluation failure as an explicit policy denial unless policy returned a deny result.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The caller-facing error may remain an authorization failure, but retained observation or audit material MUST distinguish denial from evaluation failure.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: System-service operational errors MUST NOT be treated as authority decisions or denial reasons.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The runtime MUST retain enough authority-decision material to explain allow/deny enforcement through Runtime Control observation or implementation audit logs.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: That material SHOULD include the consumer reference, the attempted operation, the target provider or route when present, and the decision identifier when present.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST compute every request and successful-response payload commitment at the Runtime-controlled invocation boundary, independently of whether authority policy requires audit retention.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST bind each root to the selected route, provider, contract, method declaration, and exact request or response type for that call.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When the decision requires retention, Runtime MUST produce the `call` audit record defined by LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST derive each retained request or response commitment from the schema-typed value at the enforcement boundary, not from an unverified root or contract identifier supplied by the provider or consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If a remote runtime is not enrolled or otherwise accepted by authority policy, the local runtime MUST NOT use it for remote-module facades or remote routes.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When a target Runtime accepts an operation forwarded by an enrolled source Runtime, the source Runtime MUST identify the module instance that it authenticated locally as the consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The target Runtime MUST verify that the consumer reference's `runtime_instance_id` matches the authenticated source Runtime identity and that active policy permits that Runtime to forward operations for consumers it owns.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: For a remote Runtime Control connection, the source Runtime MUST place the exact Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding of that consumer's `logos.runtime.module_instance_address` in the first Transport Hello `token` field.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The target Runtime MUST decode that single value, apply the ownership and forwarding checks above, and bind every Runtime Control invocation on the connection to that consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The source Runtime MUST use the connection only for that consumer and close it when it no longer authenticates that module instance as the consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A missing, empty, malformed, non-deterministic, trailing-byte, or ownership-mismatched value MUST produce Transport ProtocolError `NOT_AUTHORISED`, establish no session, and execute no Runtime Control method.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The token is a consumer reference protected by source-Runtime authentication; it is not a route ticket or grant of authority, and the Hello response token MUST be empty.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST NOT be represented using a fabricated consumer reference.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST authenticate and authorize every Runtime Control invocation independently for its consumer before applying a state mutation.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Concurrent invocations from the same or different consumers MUST NOT share consumer identity, authority decisions, or request-key scope.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST apply mutations that affect the same module instance, facade provider, route, listener, or provider export in one total order.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: That order MUST respect completion order when one invocation completes before another begins.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Each mutation MUST observe the complete result of earlier mutations in that order and MUST change its target atomically.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Operations on independent targets MAY proceed concurrently.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: For a request carrying `expected_execution_revision`, the target MUST resolve to a local module instance.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST compare that revision atomically with lifecycle acceptance and reject a mismatch without mutation, including for otherwise idempotent requests.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Concurrent lifecycle requests MUST NOT create duplicate realizations, native contexts, destruction calls, or release operations.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: A `start_module` request for an instance in `loaded` or `ready` MUST return its current module state without creating another realization or replacing retained intent or its origin.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: A `stop_module` request for an instance in `stopping` or `unloaded` MUST return its current module state and MUST NOT initiate another destruction or release.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: An explicit stop MUST cancel retained execution intent, including when the instance is already `stopping` or `unloaded`.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: If `stop_module` is ordered after an incomplete start or recovery, Runtime MUST prevent that attempt from later making the instance `ready`.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: If `start_module` is ordered while the instance is `stopping`, it MUST fail and MUST NOT schedule an implicit restart.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Once `close_route`, failure, or revocation places a route in a terminal state, a later renewal MUST fail and MUST NOT revive it.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: An observation concurrent with a mutation MAY report the complete state before or after that mutation.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: It MUST NOT combine fields from different versions of the same record.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST emit lifecycle and route-state events for one target in the same order as the corresponding committed state transitions.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Deployment documentation MUST distinguish resumption after Runtime restart from retries after execution failure.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Reconciliation MUST preserve retained origin, retry accounting, lifecycle ordering, current authority, and unresolved cleanup obligations.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: A stop caused by permission-settings reconciliation, permission withdrawal, or loss of execution authorization MUST preserve execution intent and its authenticated origin.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Loss of the Module Loader provider that owns a realization MUST NOT be treated as successful release of that realization.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Runtime MUST retain unresolved cleanup ownership until the protected realization or deployment mechanism confirms that the old execution envelope and its access to assigned state have ended.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: When the owning Loader has failed and continued realization control cannot be maintained, Runtime MUST mark affected instances as `error`, fail their routes, preserve execution intent, and arrange termination through protected host or deployment supervision.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Runtime MUST NOT realize a replacement for an affected instance while that cleanup remains unresolved.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Rebinding the Loader service MUST NOT transfer old realizations to the replacement provider.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Runtime MUST retain unresolved realization ownership and native resources until their actual uses end.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: A shared-process native realization MUST NOT be force-released by destroying referenced state or unloading code that can still execute.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Runtime prevents new consumer-initiated Runtime Control and provider-contract calls, route or binding acquisitions, and subscriptions. It transitions affected module instances to `stopping` and quiesces or closes their invocation paths, except for system-service providers and protected bindings still required for cleanup. Those providers remain usable for authorized protected cleanup operations until their dependents have been released. Their ordinary consumer invocation paths MUST remain closed.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Runtime MUST release Loader-owned realizations before quiescing and releasing or detaching their owning Loader provider through its bootstrap mechanism.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: This ordering MUST NOT extend execution or binding authority or delay required withdrawal.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Shutdown admission closure MUST NOT prevent native ownership discharge or cancellation required by LOGOS-MODULE-INTERFACE Sections 2.8 and 2.9.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: If a required service becomes unusable, Runtime MUST preserve unresolved cleanup ownership and apply the failure and supervision rules in Section 10.1.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: A deployment arranging such preparation MUST preserve required engine shutdown when the preparation service or orchestration is unavailable.

heading: 12. Large Payload Boundary
text: A profile transferring that capability MUST define authenticated recipient binding, permitted operations, lifetime, revocation, and failure behavior.

heading: 12. Large Payload Boundary
text: A path or process-local descriptor value MUST NOT be treated as authority merely because it appears in a payload.

heading: 12. Large Payload Boundary
text: A contract accepting a path MUST define whose namespace it addresses and the applicable failure when that namespace or access is unavailable.

heading: 12. Large Payload Boundary
text: A provider MUST NOT silently reinterpret a caller-local path as an unrelated resource in another execution form.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: A malformed canonical symbol name, an ambiguous module symbol family, or a missing unconditional module ABI symbol MUST also be rejected with `LOGOS_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS` during registration.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Registration MUST validate these supplied table properties without invoking module code.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Requirements that depend on the validated call surface or accepted configuration binding MUST be checked during implementation binding, before initialization or provider exposure as required by the applicable ABI rules.
